result:
Both checks pass: `bun run typecheck` is clean and `bun test` reports 6 pass / 0 fail (the `ValidationException` trace in the output is pre-existing noise from the `posts.search` 422 test, not a failure).

I added `app/Support/redirect.ts`, a small shared guard exporting `DEFAULT_REDIRECT` (`/dashboard`) and `safeRedirectPath(value, fallback)`, which only accepts a plain same-app path — a single leading `/` — and rejects anything that could leave our origin: absolute URLs with a scheme, protocol-relative `//evil.example`, backslash variants like `/\evil.example` (browsers read `\` as `/`), values whose tab/newline/CR are stripped by browsers into one of those forms (`/\t/evil.example`), any remaining control characters, and non-string or empty input — all of which fall back to the default destination. `app/Http/Controllers/Auth/LoginController.ts` now runs both redirect sources through it: `show()` sanitizes the `redirect` query parameter (with an empty-string fallback) so the login form's hidden field can never carry an off-site value back to the server, and `store()` sanitizes the resolved destination (body value, then query value, then `DEFAULT_REDIRECT`) immediately before `this.redirect()`, leaving the authentication logic itself untouched so correct credentials still sign the user in and wrong ones still throw the same `ValidationException` without a session. I also added `tests/redirect.test.ts` covering the allowed paths, each off-site variant from the report, the non-string/empty fallbacks, and the caller-supplied fallback, and noted the new `app/Support/` directory in the README's Project Structure list.
